items.before: The transhipment and transit 'Destination country' dropdowns on the reason page now offer the same places as the country of origin list: countries plus the places within them, labelled like 'Canary Islands (Spain)', in one alphabetical order. A destination saved before this change still shows when the page is reopened.
items.after:
The 'Destination country' dropdowns on the reason page have changed.

This covers the transhipment dropdown and the transit dropdown.

They now offer the same places as the country of origin list:

- countries
- the places within them, labelled like 'Canary Islands (Spain)'
- all in one alphabetical order

A destination saved before this change still shows when the page is reopened.

items.before: Destination country selects offer reference-data's countries and their subdivisions
items.after: Destination country dropdowns offer the countries from reference data, and the places within them

items.before: Before, the transit country search offered a 31-country list with no places within countries. Now it offers the same countries and places as country of origin, each place named with its country, for example 'Canary Islands (Spain)'. A country not on the list is still refused with 'Select countries from the list'.
items.after:
Before, the transit country search offered a list of 31 countries.

It had no places within countries.

Now it offers the same countries and places as country of origin.

Each place is named with its country, for example 'Canary Islands (Spain)'.

A country not on the list is still refused with 'Select countries from the list'.

items.before: Transit country search offers the GBNAG_SPS_EX countries and their subdivisions
items.after: Transit country search offers the countries on the 'GBNAG_SPS_EX' list, and the places within them

items.before: Before, ports were listed by name alone, mixing airports and seaports, with names in capitals first. Now the port of entry search, both port of exit dropdowns and plants' place of landing list show airports, then seaports, then rail ports, each A to Z ignoring capitals. Port of exit options now read like port of entry ones, for example 'Holyhead Port - GB HLY'. The port of exit lists still offer every port, because the master data has no 'approved for animals' flag.
items.after:
Before, ports were listed by name alone.

- Airports and seaports were mixed together.
- Names in capitals came first.

Now these lists show airports, then seaports, then rail ports:

- the port of entry search
- both port of exit dropdowns
- plants' place of landing list

Each group runs A to Z, ignoring capitals.

Port of exit options now read like port of entry ones, for example 'Holyhead Port - GB HLY'.

The port of exit lists still offer every port.

This is because the master data has no 'approved for animals' flag.

items.before: Port lists ordered airports, then seaports, then rail, from MDM's port type, with the port of exit reading and ordering like the port of entry, in animals and plants
items.after: Port lists in animals and plants show airports, then seaports, then rail. The order comes from the port type in the master data (MDM). The port of exit now reads and is ordered like the port of entry.

items.before: Before, local and development environments used a short hand-kept list of 31 countries and 78 ports. Now they serve the full master data lists, about 250 countries and every port with its type, the same content as the test environment. The INS address book's country dropdown offers the full country list instead of four typed-in countries. Traders on the live service see no difference; anyone reviewing on a local or development environment will.
items.after:
Before, local and development environments used a short, hand-kept list of:

- 31 countries
- 78 ports

Now they serve the full master data lists:

- about 250 countries
- every port, with its type

This is the same content as the test environment.

The INS address book's country dropdown now offers the full country list.

Before, it offered four typed-in countries.

Traders on the live service see no difference.

Anyone reviewing on a local or development environment will see the difference.

items.before: The stub's countries and ports match real MDM, and every captured country and port fixture is recaptured from it
items.after: The stand-in service's (stub's) countries and ports match the real master data (MDM). Every saved test copy of the country and port data (fixture) is captured again from it.
